These records explain the choices behind Offing's architecture, data format, contracts, and
policy. Each one is accepted unless a later record supersedes it, or unless its status says
otherwise. Records are numbered in the order they were written; this page groups them by theme.
Add Go as a first-class detector ecosystem
Add evidence-backed Go runtime, toolchain, and direct-module lifecycle detection through the existing detector SDK, without requiring the Go toolchain or network access at scan time.
Detect end-of-life container base images from Dockerfiles and Compose files
detector that reports base-image references whose release line has a vendor-published end of life.
Detect removed and deprecated Kubernetes APIs in manifests, Helm charts, and kustomizations
pairs the Kubernetes project has documented as deprecated or no longer served.
Detect end-of-support JDK releases and relocated Maven dependencies in JVM projects
detector for pinned or targeted JDKs and Maven coordinates that a vendor or maintainer has documented as out of support or moved.
Detect unsupported Rust toolchains and abandoned or yanked crates
detector that reads Cargo and toolchain files and reports lifecycle risks an authoritative source states.
Detect unsupported .NET targets and deprecated NuGet packages
detector for unsupported .NET SDK/runtime lines and deprecated NuGet packages with publisher evidence.
Detector maturity levels and the evidence to move between them
— with fixed evidence floors (fixtures, corpus size, precision, recall) to move between them.
detector that reports only image lifecycle risks the platform's authoritative documentation explicitly states.
Corpus fetch strategy: sparse checkout, concurrency 16
Default the public-repository corpus to sparse checkout at concurrency 16, with cache invalidation keyed to detector input declarations.
Key lifecycle rules by PURL and VERS with provenance
format keyed by Package URL and VERS, with provenance on each rule.
Draft lifecycle rules with importers; never write the registry
Let importers draft rules from one authoritative source; a person reviews every draft and changes
Ship lifecycle data as a versioned, content-addressed bundle
Publish and consume lifecycle data as an
document separate from the code release.
Record announced end-of-life dates that have not happened yet
event for announced future ends, reported at low severity and promoted by a reviewed change after the date.
CLI exit codes and error codes
Map failures to five fixed classes and exit codes: policy 1, usage 2, data 3, parse 4, internal 5.
Do not read OpenEoX documents yet; keep CLE as the interchange target
Scans never read OpenEoX; do not ingest it until the Core Schema is final, and keep CLE as the standards interchange path.
License the lifecycle dataset under CC BY 4.0
and first-party schemas in the data-only package under CC BY 4.0; keep the rest of the repository Apache-2.0.
symbol shape that matches a call by name on any receiver inside a class that directly subclasses
Publish a self-contained MCP output schema
before the MCP server advertises a tool's schema and throw when one cannot resolve; same-document references stay, and sibling keywords win over the inlined target.
Split the MCP server into one file per tool
Give each MCP tool its own file under
, list them in a small registry, and prove with a
snapshot that no advertised name, description, input schema, output schema, or annotation changed.
Require the retrieval date on every lifecycle source
required in registry v2, backfill every bundled record, and let the importer runner stamp the run date so every finding shows when its source was read.
Recommend a release line from bundled data only
: the newest unended line whose end date is at least 180 days away, from bundled rules only;
Add Deno and Elixir to the public validation schema
to the published corpus ecosystem enum when those detectors gain a public corpus. The change is additive.
Publish the detector limits in the SDK
type so the file-size, depth, and vendored-directory bounds are part of the typed detector contract and conformance reads them from there.
Ship v0.8.0 (adoption) and v0.9.0 (visibility) before v1
Ship adoption then visibility before v1, with usage before attention, and record post-v1 ideas as unscheduled epics.
Privacy-first adoption metrics; opt-in telemetry only after v1
Keep product telemetry off by default forever as the default; any opt-in comes only after a separate post-v1 decision.
Ship adoption and visibility as one release, with one launch
Merge v0.9.0 into v0.8.0 and replace the three mini-launches with one launch that follows the release.
Define reference quality as measurable, enforced criteria
Define eight quality criteria, each enforced by a failing check; zero new debt; existing debt allowlisted with an owner and an expiry of 2027-01-26.
Lint with ESLint and typescript-eslint (type-aware); format with Biome; do not use Biome for typed lint or Prettier for format.
Document the public API and enforce it with lint
Put a behavior-focused doc comment on every public declaration and enforce it with a local ESLint rule; no contract semantics change.
Keep fixtures out of scanners' sight with neutral names
suffix and restore the real name in a temporary directory at test time; reject archives and dismissals; scanner config is a narrow fallback.
Cut scanner complexity by extracting the line masker and replacing branch chains with tables
Move the per-language literal scanner to
, dispatch readers on tables, and prove parity differentially against a build of
; the SDK export surface is unchanged.
Select corpus repositories independently of results; target 200 per ecosystem

Freeze eligibility and stack variety for all 23 buckets before scanning; retain poor results and publish honest shortfalls against 200 reviewed repositories per bucket. Accepted on maintainer merge of the PR for #2116.
CI lanes: pull request, merge queue, main, nightly, release
Five CI lanes with wall-clock budgets; one required check (
); the merge queue is the proof that lands on
Build v0.1 in TypeScript on Node.js 22 or newer, sharing one language across CLI, engine, detectors, Action, and MCP, with no hosted backend.
Generate host plugins from shared Offing assets
Keep Skill, runtime, rules, and migration behavior as canonical shared sources and generate Codex and Claude plugins from them so CI fails on drift.
Layered architecture and the allowed-imports table
Seven layers (domain, SDK, core, detectors, services, reporters, adapters) with one allowed-imports table and runtime-access rules; each epic #1990 follow-up adds its rule to the checker.
One error model with stable reason codes
